ops.title: PR 1316: enforce each row's tap time when matching runner verdicts
ops.description: Owner: PR #1316 implementation lane (agentic-judge-landing). Static review only; no tests run. Evidence: board_rows.py:686, :780 and :512; tests/test_board_rows.py:67 and :88-91. tap_verdicts fetches from the oldest approval across all rows, then tap_verdict never compares a record's time with the particular row's approval. With row A tapped at 10:00 and B at 12:00, a B verdict from 11:00 counts even though B was approved again afterwards. The fake omits record times and substitutes the query cutoff, masking this. Next executable step: retain the batch fetch but require each verdict to postdate the row's actual tap and match its approved head; give fake records real timestamps and add a two-row regression.

ops.text: A verdict older than a row's latest approval never clears that row, even when another row causes an earlier batch cutoff.
Timestamped fake records obey the same since semantics as cci.
